From Saturn's spectacular rings to Halloween fireballs and a space station flyover, there are plenty of celestial treats in store this Halloween. Here's when and where to look.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

There could be more than just ghosts and ghouls lurking in the skies this Halloween! From Saturn's spectacular rings to shooting stars and even a space station flyover, the night sky has a few treats of its own in store for U.S. skywatchers on Oct. 31.

Based on the latest national forecast, skies will be mainly clear on Saturday evening over most of New York State, northeast Pennsylvania, northern New Jersey and New England as well as a swath of the southern and central Great Plains, central Rockies, a portion of the Pacific Northwest and central and south Florida, as costumed kids arrive at the door looking for candy or some other Halloween treat.

Temperatures will be mostly in the chilly 40s across the Northeast US, upper 50s and 60s for the nation's midsection, warm 70s to near 80 for the southern US, including Florida and the Gulf Coast, and 40s for much of the western US. Unfortunately, a storm moving across the nation's heartland may spell rainy skies for parts of Iowa and Nebraska, south to the Gulf Coast.

For those blessed with a generally fair evening, there will be views of mid-autumn stars and constellations plus a bright planet shining prominently in the early evening sky. If you plan to accompany children around your neighborhood, you might want to enlighten them by pointing out some of those objects that will be visible in the sky. Better yet, if you have a telescope, give your visitors a treat of a different kind: Give them a close-up view of some of those celestial sights.

At around 7 p.m. local time, tell your young audience to make a clenched fist with their hands and then hold them out at arm's length. Now, tell them to go "two fists" up from the east-southeast horizon and they will see a bright star, shining with a yellow-white hue. Now, direct your telescope toward that "star" and when you gaze through the eyepiece, you will not be looking at a star at all . . . but a planet!

This sixth planet out from the sun, just might be the most beautiful of all. Its rings are still readily evident, although currently they appear somewhat edge-on with the south face tilted only about 6 and a half degrees to our line of sight. A telescope magnifying 30-power will bring them out; they appear to bisect the ball of the planet. While this is far from their appearance compared to other years, the view should still look impressive to those who have never seen the ringed planet for themselves.

Because they are active over Halloween, the Taurid meteor shower is sometimes called the "Halloween Fireballs." The bits of debris that make up the Taurids are a little larger than average, so they can result in brighter meteors and even fireballs, or exploding meteors (called bolides), that streak across the sky and leave incandescent trains in their wake. While they are most active during the second week of November, a few forerunners can show up on Halloween night, darting from out of the east-northeast part of the sky. So, if you or your young visitors see something resembling a flare from a Roman candle sweeping majestically across the evening sky, it may very well be a Taurid meteor.

Not the International Space Station, but the Tianhe-1 core module, the first module to launch of the Tiangong space station. It was launched into orbit on 29 April 2021, as the first launch of the final phase of the Tiangong program, part of the China Manned Space Program (Project 921). On Halloween evening, Tianhe-1 will be following a track from Chicago to New York at an altitude of 240 miles (385 km) and should be readily visible to the naked eye across the Northeast US within a few minutes of 7 p.m. EDT, wherever skies are reasonably clear.

The Tiangong Space Station should appear to resemble a very bright star moving across the sky on a general west-to-east course. For places near and along the flight path, the Space Station will appear to pass almost directly overhead. For those situated south of the track, Tiangong will reach its highest point above the northern horizon; those situated north of the track will see the station peak high in the south.

If you see it, tell your young viewers that three astronauts are currently living and working aboard the Tiangong Space Station, of which the Tianhe core module serves as the main living quarters. If you would like specific details on when and where to see the Space Station from your hometown, check out Heavens-Above, a non-profit website and mobile application that tracks satellites, the International Space Station (ISS), comets, and astronomical events in real time.

Another website that provides live information, including an orbit map on Tianhe-1, is NY2O.com. Check its menu list on the right side of the page and look for the blue box: "10-Day Predictions for CSS (Tianhe-1)."

In the September 2019 issue of The Astronomical League Magazine "Reflector," author Richard W. Schmude Jr., offered some tips for those who plan to do public outreach for astronomy on Halloween:

"Firstly, children sometimes grab or touch the eyepiece, so use an inexpensive one. I gently warn children not to touch the telescope. In my area, parents have learned to tell their children not to touch the telescope. In some cases, a child will grab the eyepiece, causing the telescope to shift. For this reason, a Dobsonian telescope with a good finderscope is a good choice for Halloween outreach. A small stool or booster ladder may help very small viewers. Sometimes, parents hold their children up to look through the eyepiece. One may also place a monitor-connected video camera in the telescope and people can easily see the object on a screen." "Finally," adds Mr. Schmude, "I have my bag of goodies next to my telescope so that the children get two treats!"

Whatever your weather, Happy Halloween from all of us at Space.com!

#732. Warner Records Nashville Lays Off Five, Including EVP of Marketing Victoria Mason

Others affected include senior vp of publicity Fount Lynch and vp of radio Anna Cage.

Warner Records Nashville laid off five staff members on Tuesday (Nov. 3), Billboard has confirmed, including executive vp of marketing Victoria “Torie” Mason and senior vp of publicity Fount Lynch.

Mason joined Warner out of Nashville in 2011, starting as director of research & analytics before moving up the ranks. Lynch joined Warner Nashville in 2022, having previously served in roles at Red Light, Sony Music and Universal Music Group.

Other affected staffers include vp of radio Anna Cage, West Coast manager of Warner Artist Relations Jenna Johnson and regional manager of radio Kayla Burnett.

It’s unclear whether the layoffs are related to the $300 million in annual cost cuts announced by Warner Music Group (WMG) CEO Robert Kyncl last year. In a company-wide memo released in July 2025, Kyncl wrote that layoffs would account for $170 million of the planned cuts. “Many changes will be implemented in the next three months, with the remainder in fiscal 2026,” he wrote at the time. He characterized the reductions as “the remaining steps in our plan to help future-proof the company and unlock the next era of growth,” adding that the money saved would be reinvested in A&R and M&A.

WMG has instituted several rounds of layoffs since Kyncl assumed the role of CEO at the top of 2023, including a 4% staff cut that March, a 10% cut in 2024 and a restructuring at Atlantic Music Group (AMG) later that year, followed by cuts in AMG’s promotion department in August 2025. In July 2025, Warner Music Nashville, which reports through Warner Records, let go of four staffers amid a realignment of Warner Records’ marketing and commerce teams.

A representative for Warner Records Nashville did not respond to Billboard‘s request for comment by press time.

#731. England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or

The England captain ends his country's 25-year wait for the prestigious award after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season, beating competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

England captain Harry Kane won the men's Ballon d'Or for the first time on Monday, becoming the first English player to receive the prestigious football award since 2001.

The 33-year-old Bayern Munich striker was honored at a ceremony at the London Palladium after scoring 73 goals in 65 appearances for club and country last season.

The Ballon d'Or, awarded by French magazine France Football, is one of football's most prestigious individual honors, recognizing the world's best players.

The last English player to win the award was former Liverpool striker Michael Owen, who claimed the prize 25 years ago.

Kane's remarkable goalscoring record helped Bayern Munich secure a German league and cup double last season.

The former Tottenham Hotspur forward also led England to the World Cup semifinals, the country's best finish since winning the tournament in 1966.

Kane has finished as the Bundesliga's leading scorer for three consecutive seasons. He was also Europe's top club goalscorer during the 2025-26 campaign.

At Monday's ceremony, Kane thanked his Bayern Munich teammates for their support.

"Without you guys (his Bayern Munich team-mates) and the rest of the team it wouldn't be possible, the way you guys push me, the way we compete. So thank you very much," he said.

Kane also paid tribute to his former club Tottenham Hotspur, which he joined at the age of 11, as well as his England teammates and family.

"To my wife Kate, my best friend. We've been through ups and downs. You are my biggest support and I felt like you wanted this more than me," he said.

Reflecting on his career, Kane encouraged young footballers to pursue their ambitions despite setbacks.

"I hope my journey, it wasn't straightforward, I didn't go straight to the top, I had to experience a lot of loan moves and fight my way to get to where I am now. I hope that can give you inspiration."

Kane faced strong competition from Barcelona's Spanish teenager Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid's French forward Kylian Mbappe.

He joins Stanley Matthews, Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Owen among the English players to have won the award.

Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas claimed the women's Ballon d'Or for the third time in her career, having previously won the award in 2021 and 2022.

The 32-year-old was recognized after a successful season with Barcelona, winning the treble and scoring 21 goals across all competitions.

Putellas also played a key role in Barcelona's Champions League triumph, contributing seven goals and seven assists during the campaign.

She joined English club London City Lionesses in July after spending 14 years at Barcelona.

Her victory ended a run of three consecutive Ballon d'Or wins by fellow Spaniard Aitana Bonmatí.

Barcelona's Lamine Yamal won the Kopa Trophy for the best young male player for the third consecutive year, while his teammate Vicky Lopez claimed the women's award for the second year running.

Barcelona coach Pere Romeu was named women's coach of the year, while Spain manager Luis de la Fuente won the men's coaching award.

Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon received the men's Yashin Trophy, with Cata Coll winning the women's equivalent.

Barcelona was named women's club of the year, while Paris Saint-Germain took the men's award.

#730. TKO Raises Guidance Again As UFC Powers Q3 Earnings

The owner of the UFC, WWE and IMG is betting on live sports being a growth engine for years to come, with the FIFA World Cup boosting its On Location business.

TKO Group Holdings raised its guidance for the second straight quarter as the UFC and the FIFA World Cup helped propel its business in Q3.

The owner of UFC, WWE and IMG reported revenue of $1.36 billion in the quarter, up 21 percent from a year ago, with net income of $277.9 million, up from $171.1 million a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA rose by 54 percent to $555.7 million.

“Our third quarter performance reflects the secular tailwinds powering live events and experiences around the world, and TKO’s assets sit front and center of that premium ecosystem,” said Mark Shapiro, President and COO of TKO. “As we close out what we’ve called our year of execution, our decision to raise full-year guidance for the second time this year is the clearest expression of our conviction across the entire portfolio. Our business is durable and our fundamentals are solid, with the vast majority of our existing revenues locked in for the next five to seven years. Macro trends are firmly in our favor, every facet of sports consumption is pointing north, and we see substantial runway ahead.”

The company’s new guidance for full year 2026 to $5.790 billion to $5.830 billion for revenue and $2.295 billion to $2.315 billion for adjusted EBITDA.

The UFC was the biggest driver of growth, with revenue surging by 60% to $519.2 million in the quarter thanks to strong growth in media rights, sponsorships, live events and consumer products and licensing. Adjusted EBITDA rose by 72 percent to $285.3 million.

At the WWE, total revenue fell by 1 percent to $399.3 million, due to a decrease in live events and hospitality revenue, offset by increases in media rights and consumer products. Adjusted EBITDA rose 5 percent to $217.2 million.

At IMG, revenue rose 16 percent to $391.3 thanks to increases in partnerships and marketing revenue, as well as increased hospitality revenue associated with the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Adjusted EBITDA rose 89 percent to $115.9 million.

"This companion is orbiting so close to the star that it actually passes through its extended atmosphere."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Something spooky is stirring in the shadows of the infamous star Betelgeuse, a cosmic poltergeist that is disrupting the atmosphere of the red supergiant.

New radio observations have shown Betelgeuse's smaller stellar companion, Siwarha (not Betelguese Betelguese, unfortunately), cutting through the supergiant's extended atmosphere and leaving a wake in its path, like a jet boat slicing through a lake.

Because the name of this red supergiant star located about 650 light-years away from Earth, marking the shoulder of constellation Orion, is Betelgeuse, which means "the hand of al-Jawza" in Arabic, the companion was named Siwarha, meaning "her bracelet."

"This companion is orbiting so close to the star that it actually passes through its extended atmosphere," Lynn Matthews, the principal research scientist at Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) Haystack Observatory who led the new observations, said in a statement.

Using data collected from 2021 to 2026 using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array in New Mexico and the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) in Chile, Matthews and colleagues found that Betelgeuse's atmosphere stretches into an egg shape when the companion star is farthest away and rounds out when the companion passes in front of or behind it.

The same data also showed that Betelgeuse itself has largely recovered from the "Great Dimming" that made headlines in 2020. This recovery comes after the red supergiant "sneezed" in 2020, dramatically ejecting tons of gas and dust and fading to its dimmest in more than a century.

Among the long-standing mysteries of Betelgeuse, scientists have puzzled over a brightening and dimming cycle that lasts roughly 2,100 days. Recent studies pointed to a low-mass companion orbiting deep inside the star's atmosphere, and its existence was confirmed in early 2026.

Though Siwarha itself is too faint to detect directly at radio wavelengths, its influence shows up in the star's shape, the new study found. To confirm the effect, the researchers say, they will need to observe more of the companion's orbit, especially at radio frequencies that have so far been sparsely sampled.

The Next Generation Very Large Array, a planned telescope, should make this kind of monitoring far more routine, according to the team. With sharper vision, researchers could see how red supergiants like Betelgeuse shed their material as they near the end of their lives, and how a close companion might affect that process by tugging on that ejected matter.

This research is described in a paper published in The Astronomical Journal.

Sharmila Kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in Bengaluru, India. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Live Science, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston.

#728. AMC Theatres Rides Box Office Rebound to Record Revenue in Third Quarter

In a key box office recovery test, the mega-exhibitor saw theater visits, ticket and concession sales rise with Christopher Nolan's 'The Odyssey' and 'Spider Man: Brand New Day' on its screens.

AMC Entertainment on Wednesday posted sharply higher box office and revenue for its third quarter as it had Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day in its theaters.

The box office momentum will help the mega-exhibitor answer to investors whether it can leverage a steadier supply of Hollywood tentpole releases, premium screen demand and film lovers returning to the multiplex to get out from under costly debt obligations.

Overall revenue was up 31 percent to $1.71 billion, compared to $1.3 billion in the same period of 2025. That compares with the most recent second quarter when AMC saw overall revenue jump 14 percent to $1.59 billion.

AMC swung to a Q3 net income of $109.3 million, against a year-earlier net loss of $298.2 million, due mainly to non-cash charges associated with a July 2025 refinancing to fully redeem 2026 debt maturities.

The adjusted EBITDA came to $347.5 million, compared to $122.5 million and representing another quarterly record. Besides being lifted by an ongoing Hollywood box office rebound, AMC is riding a premium screen gold rush at the local multiplex by offering varied immersive auditoriums like Imax, Dolby Cinema, iSense, XL and laser projection-equipped screens.

During the latest quarter, the exhibition giant saw total admissions revenue rise to $953.5 million, compared to a year-earlier $715.1 million. Food and beverage concession revenues came to $589.5 million, up from year-earlier $451.8 million.

U.S. market attendance amounted to 52 million patrons, while international markets attendance added another 22.7 million cinema-goers at overseas venues during the third quarter. That all comes ahead of a key upcoming holiday season test for AMC as The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part Three will play on its screens.

The latest financial results follow ongoing efforts by AMC with lenders to secure flexibility to refinance its high debt load and reduce its overall interest expense. The company recently completed refinancings to push around $4 billion in debt maturities to 2031 and 2033.

Debt refinancing deals for AMC Theatres aim to give the movie theater chain breathing room on its balance sheet to pay down its long-term borrowings and ease balance sheet strains. To exchange new debt for existing borrowings, AMC typically has had to put up as collateral theaters and related intellectual property.

“After six long years navigating AMC through unchartered waters, we can finally say with relief that we have brought our ship into port,” AMC Theatres CEO Adam Aron told analysts during an after-market call. “What you are seeing now is a company proving quarter after quarter what it can achieve when an inspired movie slate combines with a powerful fleet of movie theaters.”

Earlier, in a statement that accompanied his latest quarterly results, Aron explained that financial performance was “thanks to our industry-leading loyalty programs along with the vast and growing number of AMC’s premium large format and extra large format auditoriums, combined with disciplined cost management, superb execution and the operating leverage inherent in our business.

The CEO added, “Our success was driven by a resurgent box office, market share gains in both domestic and international markets, and the achievement of all-time record revenue per patron.”

On the analyst call, Aron commented on Paramount Skydance completing its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, and touted the enlarged studio’s pledge to produce more movies with extended theatrical releases. “We’re confident that Skydance will do everything in its power to create and deliver appealing movies under both the Warner and Paramount brands going forward,” he argued.

Aron also reiterated AMC will release on its Imax screens the upcoming sequel to Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, the Brad Pitt-starrer The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. Cinemark and Regal among major chains have decided against doing their own sequel releases due to Netflix’s ultra-short two-week release window on offer.

Cliff Booth will debut in theaters on Nov. 25, then hit Netflix on Dec. 23. AMC in 2027 will have two other Netflix movies on its release slate, Narnia and Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, both of which will have “a full theatrical window,” Aron said.

He also discussed AMC using AI tools in Europe to program which movies go into which auditoriums in its theaters. “The financial implications of this, if it works, could be so significant,” he told analysts about the potential labor savings and efficiencies in better targeting cinemas with the right titles.

On the first day of his farewell tour in China, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier urged the German business community to act with confidence in the Chinese market.

"When you travel in China, you're amazed at how highly Germany and German technology are still valued here," he said in Hefei. "That's why we can act with confidence in these markets."

Steinmeier did not bring any companies with him to China as part of his delegation, as his final trip was intended to focus on culture and science.

Nevertheless, the first day of the trip in Hefei, the capital of Anhui Province, revolved primarily around the economy. Steinmeier visited the Volkswagen China Technology Company (VCTC). About three years ago, Europe's largest automaker opened a research center for electric mobility there, which today employs 3,000 people.

Johannes Volkmann, a lawmaker accompanying Steinmeier in China, warned that the German economy must not "lose its leadership in innovation."

"I'm taking this call to action with me from here to do more to improve competitive conditions at home," he said, adding that Germany must avoid creating new dependencies "by allowing innovation and value creation to take place only outside Europe."

Additional reporting by Rosalia Romaniec in Hefei.

A German court denied a defense request to end the trial of a former Ukrainian army officer who stands accused of sabotaging the Nord Stream gas pipelines.

Serhii Kuznietsov, 50, went on trial this month at the Hamburg state court, charged with causing an explosion, damaging property, disrupting public services and being an "accomplice to war crimes" by attacking civilian infrastructure.

Prosecutors accuse him of being the ringleader of the destruction, considered one of Europe's biggest acts of post-World War II sabotage. He is alleged to have carried out the explosions together with six others.

His lawyers said the charges should be dismissed, arguing that, as a former soldier, Kuznietsov was obligated by Ukrainian law not to speak for national security reasons and could face severe penalties in Ukraine if he did. They argued that, under German law, anyone who cannot speak on his or her own behalf cannot be convicted.

The Hamburg court ruled Kuznietsov's defense was not limited under German law and that freedom to testify is not limited by a foreign country's conditions of service.

The undersea explosions on September 26, 2022, damaged the Nord Stream 1 pipeline, which brought Russian natural gas to Germany until Moscow cut off supplies in August 2022.

The blasts also damaged the Nord Stream 2 pipeline, which never went into service. Germany suspended the pipeline's certification process shortly before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Italian authorities detained Kuznietsov last year. He was publicly named in extradition proceedings that led to his transfer to Germany in November.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has denied allegations that his country was involved in the pipeline blasts.

The move makes Mercedes the third big German carmaker to lower its outlook for 2026 after BMW and VW took similar steps.

Mercedes-Benz CEO Ola Kaellenius has called on German employees to work more without pay while also expanding manufacturing operations in Hungary, where he said costs are about 70% lower than in Germany.

Mercedes currently expects an adjusted car profit margin of 2% to 3% in 2026, compared to the 3% to 5% in the previous guidance.

Like many German automakers, Mercedes has faced weak sales in China. German carmakers have struggled in the world's largest car market with sluggish demand and increased competition from local manufacturers.

Mercedes vehicle deliveries in China — last year already at their lowest level since 2016 — fell a further 29% in the nine months to the end of September.

Mercedes also released third-quarter figures earlier than planned, which showed that the company generated just €172 million ($191 million) in free cash flow from its vehicle business, down on the €422 million forecast by financial market experts.

Before interest and tax, Mercedes posted an operating profit of €1.77 billion — more than double the €750 million recorded a year earlier, according to the preliminary figures. But last year's stats were significantly impacted by one-time expenses, especially related to job cuts and legal disputes.

The German agency responsible for finding a final repository for nuclear waste (BGE) has eliminated five states from its search.

Berlin, Hesse, Rhineland-Palatinate, Saxony and Saarland were deemed unsuitable for long-term radioactive waste storage.

In a report issued Tuesday, the BGE said it had limited its search to 5% of Germany, down from 25% in 2025. The federal agency aims to suggest suitable locations for final evaluation by the end of 2027.

Regions in northern, northwestern, southern and eastern Germany remain under consideration as locations for final storage facilities.

Germany's nuclear waste is currently stored in 16 above-ground interim storage facilities.

The BGE assessments evaluate regions' geological conditions and their ability to safely contain highly radioactive material. Granite, salt, and clay are generally considered potentially suitable types of rock and areas with damaged or compromised subsurface conditions, places with mines or volcanos have been active, are not eligible as final disposal sites.

Germany needs to find a repository for approximately 27,000 cubic meters of highly radioactive nuclear waste generated over more than 60 years of nuclear power generation. The site is expected to ensure safety for 1 million years. The last German nuclear power plants were decommissioned in April 2023.

BGE said its goal remains finding the site that offers the highest level of safety for highly radioactive waste.

The agency's recommendations, however, are not legally binding and it will be up to German lawmakers to determine the final disposal site.

Convicted right-wing terrorist Beate Zschäpe's request for early release from prison was denied with a court ruling that she would remain behind bars for at least nine more years.

Munich's Higher Regional Court on Tuesday set her minimum term at at least 24 years and refused to suspend the sentence to probation. By determining her guilt to be particularly severe, the court effectively ruled out her release after 15 years, which, including her time in pretrial detention, would have expired this year.

The Munich court said Zschäpe, currently 51, still had a good chance of leaving prison alive.

The decision is not yet legally binding, and the defense and the Federal Prosecutor's Office can appeal.

Zschäpe had been sentenced to life in prison in 2018 as an accomplice in the National Socialist Underground (NSU) murders that killed 10 people, mainly individuals with an immigrant background as well as a police officer.

The terror group went undetected for a decade. Zschäpe's fellow NSU members, Uwe Mundlos and Uwe Böhnhardt, injured several people with bomb attacks in Cologne and killed themselves to avoid arrest in 2011.

Under normal conditions, a convict who receives a life sentence in Germany can apply for parole after 15 years.

Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.

German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius, along with his counterparts from France, Italy, Poland and the UK, authored an op-ed calling Russia "the most acute and long-term threat to Euro-Atlantic security and stability."

In the article, published online and in Tuesday's Tagesspiegel newspaper, the defense ministers wrote they "share a deep conviction" that European countries need to do more to ensure their own security and aim to build "a stronger Europe within a stronger NATO."

The ministers, however, added that the United States would remain an "indispensable ally."

The pronouncement comes as many in Europe are wary of US President Donald Trump's commitment to the NATO military alliance.

The US leader has threatened to leave the group and to seize control of Greenland, a territory of fellow NATO member Denmark. US presidents have repeatedly called for European NATO members to contribute more to the alliance's military capabilities.

As US support for Ukraine also appears to waver, the five defense ministers reiterated their political, military and financial support for Kyiv as it fights of Russia's full-scale invasion.

"We must assert our interests in an international environment shaped by renewed great-power rivalry," Merz said.

With a view to unpredictable tariffs imposed by the United States under President Donald Trump and trade restrictions from China, Merz emphasized the stability offered by Germany and the rest of Europe.

"This is a deliberate counterpoint to what we are currently seeing. We want to do things differently, and we want to show that there is a better way," Merz said, adding that Europe sought to expand partnerships to increase free trade with open competition, reliability and a rules-based order.

He also called for increased international investment and cooperation.

"Under the federal government I lead, investment opportunities will be continuously improved," Merz said following a meeting with Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong. "I encounter a great deal of confidence here in Germany and in Europe as locations for investment."

For his part, Wong said investment in Germany and Europe would continue.

"Many of our investors, including our sovereign wealth funds, have been investing in Germany for a long time," Wong said. "They will continue to invest because they are confident that, in the long term, Germany and Europe have potential."

Merz and Wong agreed their nations would work to expand cooperation in security and defense as well as trade, investment, sustainable energy and artificial intelligence.

The waning moon shines with Jupiter, Mars and the brilliant star Regulus in the eastern sky overnight Nov. 1-2.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know.

Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky.

Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer.

Stargazers in Australia, Indonesia and a host of other island nations and territories will see the moon pass directly in front of Jupiter, hiding its light in an event known as an occultation starting at 3:45 p.m. EST (2045 GMT) on Nov. 2 , according to In-The-Sky.org. However, the exact visibility and timings depend on location.

The cosmic pile-up serves as a spectacular reminder of the scale and diversity of targets on display in the night sky. After all, the moon appears largest from our Earthly perspective, but in reality it's less than half the diameter of Mars.

Jupiter, meanwhile, is over 20 times wider than the red planet, while mighty Regulus is up to four times larger than the sun, andcould easily fit all the planets of the solar system in its vast expanse.

By moonrise on the night of Nov. 3, the lunar crescent will have leapt past Jupiter and Mars, to appear just 1 degree from the blue-white light of Regulus for viewers in the U.S. Meanwhile, viewers in several South American countries including Brazil, Peru, Argentina and Bolivia will see the moon occult Regulus beginning at 6:59 EST (1024 GMT) on Nov. 3. The exact timings for a selection of South American countries can be found below, courtesy of In-The-Sky.org.

Want to get a closer look at the moon and planets of the solar system? Then be sure to check out our picks of the best telescopes and binoculars for exploring the night sky, including the Celestron NexStar 8SE, which we rank as the best motorized telescope out there.

#722. Coach’s Loved Leather Finish Gives Cult-Classic Handbags the Heritage Treatment

The new vintage-inspired technique makes each piece one of one.

If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission.

Coach’s most-loved designs are getting an extra dose of affection with the introduction of a specialized leather finish, aptly titled Loved Leather.

To achieve this, Coach uses an innovative new treatment on either smooth or Glovetanned leather to reveal its true base color for an authentic, vintage-inspired finish. The result is the label’s best-selling styles — like the Brooklyn Shoulder Bag, the Empire Carryall and even the Margot Sandal and Margot Slingback kitten heel — with a subtly distressed look that feels entirely genuine. Related Stories Lifestyle Marilyn Monroe, Audrey Hepburn, PÖFF Garments Bring the Glitz to New Fashion Museum Near Tallinn Lifestyle Inde Navarrette, Michael B. Jordan and Yerin Ha Front David Yurman's New York-Set Holiday Campaign

Coach’s Empire Carryall collection spans from the most petite Empire 21 ($325) to the largest Empire 48 ($950+).

Smaller Brooklyn 28 also available ($350).

Equally into the Loved Leather Margot Sandal ($195), featuring an oversized buckle detail.

Thanks to their love-worn nature, each piece is completely unique. And its intentional lived-in look means you don’t have to be too precious in your day to day. As time goes on, the patina continues to develop and natural signs of wear take hold, meaning Loved Leather products only get more distinctive and special with age.

While Coach introduced Loved Leather across nearly all its categories — purses, footwear, outerwear, travel bags and small leather goods — the brand’s cult-favorite handbags are inevitably the star of the show. This includes the beloved Coach Brooklyn Shoulder Bag, the petite Teri Shoulder Bag, the oversized Soft Empire Carryall Bag 48, the east-west Empire Carryall Bag 34, the newer Kisslock Frame Bag 27 and, a versatile favorite, the Emily Shoulder Bag.

Adjustable strap extends from handbag, to shoulder to crossbody length.

Finished with two detachable straps to carry by hand or wear crossbody.

As for current accessories trends, the loved-leather look perfectly ties in to the slouchy shoulder bag moment we’re seeing this fall into winter, as structured silhouettes and hardware-heavy handbags are making way for their laid-back counterparts. These relaxed styles go hand in hand with the lived-in leather treatment seen across Coach’s messenger bags, totes and carryalls.

Also available in honey brown and chestnut brown Loved Leather, plus teak Loved Suede ($1,200).

And Loved Leather is not a one-color-fits-all situation — It comes in shades of brown, tan, black, olive and white, with both silver and brass hardware. There are even Loved Suede and Loved Denim options, two fresh takes on Coach’s signature treatment.

No one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier.

During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon. So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

NASA called the asteroid the "Great Pumpkin," while others called it the "Halloween Asteroid."

Be afraid, be very afraid... Okay, not really, but there is reason to be concerned about near-Earth objects and the time in which they are detected.

"According to the catalog of near-Earth objects (NEOs) kept by the Minor Planet Center, this is the closest currently known approach by an object this large until asteroid 1999 AN10, at about 2,600 feet (800 meters) in size, approaches at about 1 lunar distance (238,000 miles from Earth) in August 2027," NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) reported in 2015.

NASA’s Near-Earth Object Observations Program, sometimes called “Spaceguard,” works to catalog these type of objects and predicts some of their paths if they could be potentially threats to our planet. While there are no known credible impact threats to date, it doesn't mean the "Great Pumpkin," or rather a great impactor, isn't real.

As for 2015 TB145, it did return to Earth's vicinity in 2018, but at a much more distant pass of about 24 million miles (38 million kilometers), "or about a quarter the distance between Earth and the sun," according to JPL.

Maya Hawke will star in “Magic: The Gathering,” a movie version of the wildly popular trading card game.

Hawke’s role has not been disclosed. Plot details also remain under wraps, though the tabletop game is set across a multiverse of fantasy worlds and involves players who are engaged in a battle, acting as wizards known as Planeswalkers. Hawke is expected to anchor a yet-to-be-cast ensemble of actors, according to Deadline, which first reported the news. Legendary Entertainment and Hasbro Entertainment are producing the live-action movie, with Matt Johnson (“Blackberry,” “Nirvanna the Band the Show”) set to direct. “I was x&0 with good breakers going into day 2 of GP Detroit and telling myself, ‘I’m going to drop out of film school and become a pro Magic player,’” Johnson said. “Pod one I’m seated across from Rich Hoaen. #719. DNC Vice Chair: “We Had to Hit the Bottom”

A leader of the Democratic blue-nami on viral videos, the billionaire tax and how everything had to go wrong before it could go right.

The Democrats and their many supporters in Hollywood had a historic election Tuesday night, and it’s leaving some of the people who orchestrated it both celebratory and trying to learn from the results.Jane Kleeb is one such person. A vice chair of the Democratic National Committee under Ken Martin who also heads up the Association of State Democratic Committees (which basically represents the Democratic party in each state and territory), she helped lead the movement that resulted in Tuesday’s many wins.

A native Nebraskan and longtime activist, Kleeb was in a giddy mood Wednesday, and also a pragmatic one. We got on the phone with her to break everything down.First I have to ask, how much of a surprise were some of these races? A few felt on the bubble coming in but others were just shockers. Does it feel that way to you?I definitely thought we were going to win the House and the Senate back because I knew the quality of candidates and the infrastructure we were building, and I thought we would win some governors’ races and break some supermajorities at the state legislative level as well. But I didn’t know it would be to this extent — that the margins would be so wide. In some of these races it wasn’t one or two percentage points; it was five or six or more. So it was a resounding victory, not just voting against Trump.So you don’t see a lot of these as “anti” votes.When I was watching some pundits [on cable news] last night people were pontificating saying this was just a rebuke to Trump. And no question it was. But it was also because Democratic organizers everywhere and candidates who looked and sounded like their communities and were also fighters. So it was all of those factors.Of course, you’ve tried to do that before. What changed?I think it’s because our candidates this cycle thought they had nothing to lose. That Donald Trump was such a threat to democracy that they were putting everything on the field and because of that it happened all across the country not just in targeted battleground states.You say nothing to lose. In your mind did you need to hit rock bottom — did 2024’s calamity enable this?There’s no question we had a major reality-check as a party in 2024. And even in 2016. We felt like we recovered some footing in 2020 but not enough to carry us. We saw that with the divisions over keeping Biden as the nominee or switching candidates 100 days out in [2024]. And that’s a picture of where we were as a party, that we couldn’t find our voice, we couldn’t find our footing. We couldn’t figure out how to communicate to the American people all of the good things we were doing. So we hit the bottom. We had to hit the bottom. When Trump won again we saw with so many of the communities that we frankly took for granted — Black voters and young voters and Latino voters — they saw Trump as a change agent and someone who would break up the status quo. And obviously he didn’t deliver on any of that, so we picked back up and said “actually we’re the party fighting for change to level the playing field.” And voters received that message.That certainly happened across the Midwest and the South. But a lot of our readers are in California, where that didn’t happen — it looks like the billionaire’s tax is going to fail pretty badly. Why couldn’t you make that case to Californians?If the tax fails it could be for a lot of reasons. Maybe it’s that people don’t like taxes, it could be that.Honestly the way it was laid out on the ballot was also confusing — you basically had a billionaire tax and a ban on a billionaire tax right next to each other, both just looking like a property tax.I think it could also have been that. I definitely still believe people are deeply frustrated by the billionaire class and want to see accountability from billionaires. So maybe it’s not a tax but maybe it’s stopping giveaways at the federal level. There are other ways to get that accountability.One thing that struck me about the election is that unlike in past party sweeps — say, the Democrats in 2008 with Obama — there was no central charismatic figure around which all these House and Senate and local races coalesced. That you did it bottom-up instead of top-down.

The difference this time was definitely the story of a team instead of a lead actor. And I think that’s where the party shines. When rely on one person to carry us through we’re going to lose that battle. That happened with President Obama during his terms. We lost 1,500 seats at the local level over his eight years because we weren’t investing in state and local infrastructure; we got so wrapped up in “Obama.” So I think we learned the hard lesson that it’s this infrastructure model that works. And we saw that this time.What would you say was the biggest surprise last night?Symone Sanders, who is from [here in] Nebraska had been talking about Mississippi. So I went down and visited. I thought ’this was a state where it could happen, but not this cycle.’ But that was a mistake. We had Brandon Presley, [a moderate Democrat] who almost won [for governor in 2023]. But we didn’t give the resources to get over the finish line. And to see what Scott [Colom] has done without those resources — if this happens [Colom is currently leading his opponent Cindy Hyde-Smith by a few dozen votes with 44,000 ballots outstanding] it’s from the sheer grit of Scott and the Democratic Party there and the candidates down-ballot.And the viral videos were insane — he did that whole pick “another protein/pick another Senator” bit to troll Hyde-Smith’s line from a debate. I don’t think I can remember a political ad as subtly effective and smile-inducing as that.He’s been great. And it does make me feel like, damn, we should have known.You do have limited resources, though, and I wonder how you spread that out now that so many states seem to be in play, places like Kansas and Nebraska and Texas and South Carolina and maybe even Alaska. It seemed a lot easier when certain red states were just automatically out of bounds. Does this indeed make where to spend your money more complicated?What is very clear from the amount of money raised this cycle is that we don’t have limited resources. There’s plenty of money in the political system. What you will hear from me and Chair Martin and many who live and work in our 57 states and territories is we can and should have permanent infrastructure everywhere, no exceptions, year-round.You don’t think there are simply some states too far gone to justify Democrats spending money in — that if, say, Florida couldn’t elect a Democratic Senator or governor in this climate, maybe it’s beyond hope for the party?

I think this is absolutely the wrong way to look at it. Colorado was red not that long ago, and then we began organizing and getting young people to vote. Georgia was red not that long ago and now look at it. [SZ: Both those states saw large influxes of Democrats from other states that Florida has not seen.] I grew up in Florida and it was a swing state. We’re starting to organize there. You have places like Colorado and Mississippi where there are cities that are blue and then you spread out to the suburbs and beyond making inroads there. Florida has that too. I think you’ll begin to see things shift significantly in places like Florida and Nebraska [where the party came close to defeating a Republican this cycle with an independent Senate candidate] as we head into 2028.Speaking of looking ahead, now the Democrats have to govern. And they have to govern with moderates and progressives and far-left activists in the came caucus. We see here in Hollywood the rifts that can happen even among Democrats — we see it, and I’m kidding but not kidding, all too well unfortunately. How do you ensure those rifts don’t happen in the next two years?I think having progressives and moderates gives us an advantage because we’ll have durable long-lasting policies that all kinds of Americans will embrace. Because the American people have all those different views too. People look at these disparities as a risk, but I see them as an advantage.

#718. Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker

Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.

To most Bayern Munich fans under the age of 40, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge was the club CEO who regularly spoke his mind. Fans with longer memories, or a better grasp of Bavarian football history, recall Rummenigge as one of the club's all-time great players. He was also the last Bayern man to win the Ballon d'Or — in 1981. The last Bundesliga player to win was Borussia Dortmund's Matthias Sammer, in 1996.

That long drought ended on Monday, with Harry Kane, born 12 years after Rummenigge's win, picking up the 2026 trophy at a ceremony held, as a one-off, in his native London.

"I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special,” he said on stage.

Not many people would have thought it, and maybe even I wouldn't have thought I'd be this far," Kane later told British sports streaming plaftorm DAZN.

Lamine Yamal, the prodigious Barcelona and Spain forward who won the Euros at 16, finished third. At the end of the 2025-26 season, on which the award is judged, Yamal won the World Cup with Spain as well as the La Liga title. Kylian Mbappe came in second.

Kane's 73 goals for club and country last season made for a strong case, and the Bundesliga's most expensive signing of all time has already racked up 156 goals in 159 games for the serial German champions. But it's not just the numbers that tell the story, according to his club coach.

"People in England saw him as a goalscorer during his time playing there," Vincent Kompany said of Kane last season. "We've seen other qualities too, such as his footballing intelligence. We can appreciate that now — it was perhaps somewhat underestimated in England. He's like a fine wine that improves with age. I also enjoy that aspect of his game."

Kane continues to improve at 33, a point when many footballers start to regress. Though he is helped by being more reliant on guile and technique than pace, Kane's professionalism is key to staying at the top, according to his Bayern teammate Serge Gnabry.

"He always has the right attitude, always leads the way and sets the tone," Gnabry said ahead of Bayern's 2-2 draw in the Champions League against Arsenal last week. "He never strays from his path, helps the team with his performance and is a top-tier player."

Kane scored a penalty in that match and provided a sensational pass from which Alphonso Davies scored Bayern's opener, another reminder of his all-round game. "The pass was one of my best ones," Kane said after the match. "I knew Phonzy [Davies] would be able to get there with his speed. Whatever I can do to help the team, I'll do. At the moment, it seems to be with assists more than goals."

That attitude has been with Kane from the start. His first-ever coach, Dave Bricknell, from Ridgeway Rovers, an amateur club in northeast London, told DW after Kane joined Bayern from Spurs in 2023: "Harry's mentality is his greatest strength. He doesn't let anything worry him. If he misses a chance, he doesn't care — he will go and score from another chance."

His England coach, Thomas Tuchel, has also emphasized Kane's leadership. "He is the first one to push everyone, and that is his mindset, and he became a very, very hardworking forward on top of his finishing skills, Tuchel said in September as Kane extended his England goal-scoring record against the Czech Republic. "He is a complete package."

There are detractors who point to perceived "stat-padding," or scoring against inferior opponents in international qualifiers and in the Bundesliga, where there are fewer elite teams and a lot less money, than in England. Though Kane's ratio of 213 goals in 320 games in the Premier League is a little off his Bundesliga stats, it bears comparison with any other player in the history of the league.

Kane winning the award is also a boost in profile for the Bundesliga, which has been unable to keep pace, both commercially and on the pitch, with other top European leagues of late, particularly the Premier League and La Liga.

Winning it in a league outside of England or Spain perhaps makes Kane's feat even greater. Other than Ousmane Dembele, who won it last year after Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League win, and Lionel Messi, a serial Ballon d'Or winner, the last player to take the Ballon d'Or for a season played outside England or Spain was was Kaka at AC Milan in 2007, when Italy's Serie A was considered a stronger league.

Kane's career hasn't been straightforward, something he admitted in his speech. After signing his first senior contract with Spurs in July 2010, he was sent out on various loans to lower league sides between 2011-2013 without ever making a huge impression.

"My journey wasn't straightforward. I wasn't the kid who went straight to the top. I had to experience the downs, I had a lot of loan moves, I had to fight my way to be the very best right now, and I hope that can give you determination as well," Kane said in his speech.

For former teammate Jermain Defoe, who also coached Kane at Spurs, those experiences were formative.

"You have to show a resilience. It's not easy when you go out on loan, it can feel like you're being rejected by the club that you are at, which isn't the case," he told DW in 2023, before adding that Kane's ability was always clear.

"When he joined up with the [Tottenham] first team, you could see the potential," Defoe said. "He was always a good finisher, always hit the ball clean. … With Harry you already knew, he had that natural instinct and always felt comfortable in front of goal."

Those goals have, after a failure to win a trophy in England, led to two Bundesliga titles and a German Cup. But success with England remains elusive after a 2026 World Cup exit in the semifinals. Kane will be 35 by the time of the next Euros, in the UK and Ireland in 2028, and has a deal with Bayern until the following year. His form since joining Bayern suggests that he could get better still.

This article was first published on October 22, 2026. It was updated on October 27 after Harry Kane won the 2026 Ballon d'Or.

On Episode 234 of This Week In Space, Tariq Malik and Mike Wall are joined by Than Putzig of the Planetary Science Institute about a NASA-backed payload bound for the Marius Hills Pit on the moon.

In our ongoing quest to develop a moon base, could we possibly utilize the area beneath the surface of the moon in order to make the moon habitable? Could Marius Hills Pit, a roughly 50-meter-wide opening that may lead into a lunar lava tube, become the Moon's first living habitat for humans?

Putzig explains how geophysical instruments on a rover could detect hidden voids beneath the surface and measure the size of these lava tubes. We also ask Than how these lava tubes form, what a follow-up robotic explorer could reveal, and how this research fits alongside NASA’s Artemis plans for a south polar moon base. Join us!

Tariq is an Eagle Scout (yes, he earned the Space Exploration merit badge), a Space Camp veteran (4 times as a kid, once as an adult), and has taken the ultimate "vomit comet" ride while reporting on zero-gravity fires. #716. ‘Club Kid,’ ‘Queen at Sea’ Earn Top Prizes at Philadelphia Film Festival; 35th Edition Sets All-Time Attendance Record (EXCLUSIVE)

Lance Hammer’s “Queen at Sea” and Jordan Firstman‘s “Club Kid” earned top honors at the Philadelphia Film Festival, taking home the narrative jury prize and the narrative audience award, respectively. This year’s festival, which marked the 35th edition, drew the highest attendance in PFF history.

In his recent cover story with Variety, Firstman shared his excitement that “Club Kid,” despite centering on the granular world of New York’s queer clubbing scene, touched a diverse range of movie fans as an intimate family drama about a long-lost son and a young father coming into his own. Related Stories Netflix Steampunk Western 'Bass x Machina' Is a Crackling Mix of Fantasy and Reality: TV Review Jamie Lee Curtis, Téa Leoni and Tim Daly Lead NBC’s Refreshing and Witty Sitcom 'Newlyweds': TV Review

“It’s been amazing to see the kinds of people that relate to this film, but it really is a movie about growth,” Firstman said. “In Telluride, I watched a 75-year-old conservative man leave the theater in tears. Then we took it to the New York Film Festival, which I was very nervous to do, and showed it to the 35-year-olds who do drugs. I built the story to work on levels, with the top being a layer of warmth that feels like a hug. I explore some of my more transgressive ideas beneath the surface. If you don’t get it, there’s still a story that will make you laugh and feel something.”

Other PFF honorees included Liese’s “Seized,” which won the jury award for best documentary feature. Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor’s devastating Gaza doc “Naza” and David Greaves, Liani Greaves and William Greaves’ intimate look-back at the Harlem Renaissance, “Once Upon a Time in Harlem,” shared the documentary audience prize. “Big Phan,” a biopic about the Phillie Phanatic, earned the audience award for local feature.

Philadelphia-area filmmaking award winners were “The Haunting of Pennhurst,” from directors Mike Attie, Katarina Poljak and Nathan Stenberg, which won best Filmadelphia feature. Dana Nachman’s “The Second Life of Freddie Nole” took home best Filmadelphia short.

Rounding out the jury categories was Stephen P. Neary’s “Living with a Visionary,” which won best short film. PFF also honored actor and filmmaker Tim Blake Nelson with the artistic achievement in directing award for his new feature, “The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd.”

See a full list of audience and jury award winners below.

#715. Scarlett Johansson Breaks Silence on ‘The Batman Part II’ Role: “It Was Very Hard to Figure Out”

The actress' character in Matt Reeves' sequel to DC Studios' 2022 film has yet to be revealed.

Scarlett Johansson is opening up about her mysterious role in The Batman Part II, revealing that the part gave her “a lot of existential angst.”

In an interview with Entertainment Tonight, published Wednesday, the actress was asked about her upcoming projects, The Exorcist: Martyrs and The Batman Part II, and which role pushed her furthest out of her comfort zone.

“Probably the role in The Batman,” she responded. “It gave me a lot of existential angst for some reason.”

Johansson went on to explain that the role was particularly difficult to figure out, though she wasn’t sure exactly why. Related Stories Lifestyle Skyler Gisondo on His Style Evolution, Landing His First Fashion Campaign With Bonobos and Playing Ariana Grande's Fiancé in 'Focker-in-Law' TV Earl Barret, 'Too Close for Comfort' Writer and Producer, Dies at 94

“It was very hard to figure out. I don’t know why, whether it was just the role or was just where I’m in my life, or what’s going on, but it was just hard to crack it. And that’s all I can say about it. It was a tough role in a lot of ways,” she added.

Director Matt Reeves confirmed in May that Johansson would be joining the sequel to his 2022 film, which stars Robert Pattinson as Bruce Wayne/Batman. However, details about the character she will portray have yet to be revealed.

In addition to Johansson, new additions to the sequel’s cast include Sebastian Stan, Charles Dance as well as Brian Tyree Henry and Sebastian Koch. (See the full cast here.)

Production on The Batman Part II briefly paused in October after Reeves stepped away to attend to a family matter, according to DC Studios. Later that month, Steven Soderbergh (Ocean’s Eleven, Traffic) stepped in, with the studio’s support, to help Reeves complete the final stretch of principal photography.

The Batman Part II is currently scheduled to hit theaters Feb. 18, 2028.

#714. Best Memes and TikToks After Midterms’ Blue Wave, From Regina George to ‘The Office’ References

After Democrats flipped the U.S. House and Senate, some people took to social media to express their euphoric feelings as well as take jabs at Donald Trump.

The internet has not been disappointed with its reactions to the blue wave during the 2026 Midterms on Tuesday, when Democrats flipped both the U.S. House and Senate.

It was a tough night for Republicans as Democrats flipped Senate seats in several battleground and ruby-red states, including Texas, North Carolina, South Carolina, Kansas, Iowa, Ohio and Maine, and held on to seats in Georgia and Michigan. As for the House, they also flipped more than two dozen districts.

As conservatives grapple with what went wrong, liberals are reveling in their big wins, specifically with memes and TikTok flooding social media. Some people are even using clips from popular movies and TV shows — such as The Office, Avengers: Endgame, Breaking Bad, Mean Girls and Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby — to express their euphoric feelings as well as take jabs at President Donald Trump, who is undoubtedly frustrated. Related Stories Midterms 2026 DNC Vice Chair: "We Had to Hit the Bottom" News Hollywood Celebrates Democrats' Midterm Sweep: "The Trump Regime Is Over"

Some are also taking a moment to shout out some of the notable Democratic winners, including James Talarico, who won the Texas Senate race; Senator Jon Ossoff, who was reelected in Georgia; Abdul El-Sayed, who won the Michigan Senate Race; and Annie Andrews, who won the Senate race in South Carolina; among others. Others are celebrating history-making wins, such as Chris Pappas becoming the first openly gay man elected to the Senate and Keisha Lance Bottoms becoming the first-ever Black woman elected governor in any state with her win in Georgia.

Below, The Hollywood Reporter is rounding up the most memorable social media reactions.

#713. Box Office: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ to Lead With $30 Million Opening Weekend, ‘Cat in the Hat’ Aims for $20 Million Debut

“Godzilla Minus Zero” should stomp to the top of box office charts, with the Kaiju sequel on track to earn a strong $30 million from 3,254 North American theaters in its opening weekend.

The action adventure will tower over fellow newcomers including Warner Bros. Animation’s “The Cat in the Hat” and Searchlight’s dark buddy comedy “Wild Horse Nine,” starring John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell and directed by Martin McDonagh. “The Cat in the Hat” is aiming for second place with $20 million to $25 million from 4,000 domestic venues. “Wild Horse Nine” is targeting $5 million to $7 million from just 1,000 screens. Related Stories Netflix Steampunk Western 'Bass x Machina' Is a Crackling Mix of Fantasy and Reality: TV Review Phoebe Bridgers Makes L.A.'s Intuit Dome Into an Intimate Space Full of Love, Grief, Light Shows, 'Peter Pan' Cosplay and a Great Billie Eilish Duet: Concert Review

“Godzilla Minus Zero” will build on the excitement from 2023’s “Godzilla Minus One,” a sci-fi epic that surprised in the U.S. with $11.4 million domestically to start. With great reviews and a lack of competition (it debuted during Hollywood’s actors and writers strike), “Godzilla Minus One” powered to $57 million to stand as the highest-grossing live-action Japanese film in North America. Globally, the film earned $113 million and won a visual effects Oscar.

Produced by Japan’s Toho and distributed in the U.S. by GKids, “Godzilla Minus Zero” should overindex on premium large formats; it’s the first Japanese production ever filmed for Imax. Directed by Takashi Yamazaki, the movie takes place two years after the prior installment as Godzilla regenerates and resurfaces to combat a new monster that’s tormenting postwar Japan. Reviews have been overwhelmingly positive, with Variety’s chief film critic Owen Gleiberman calling the sequel an “even grander follow-up to ‘Godzilla Minus One.'”

“Cat in the Hat” is tracking a much lower opening than prior animated Dr. Seuss adaptations. By comparison, 2018’s “The Grinch” opened to $67 million, and 2012’s “The Lorax” opened to $70 million, neither adjusted for inflation. Sure, the theatrical landscape has changed dramatically since those films were released. However this spring’s “Hoppers,” an original offering from Pixar, managed to debut to $45 million. Recently, though, animated movies based on popular IP have enjoyed long theatrical lives, and the studio is hoping “Cat in the Hat” performs similarly to Sony’s 2024 adventure “Garfield,” which bowed to $23 million and powered to $91 million domestically and $257 million globally.

“Cat in the Hat” will rely on word-of-mouth, as well as overseas audiences, to achieve the staying power necessary to justify its $92 million production budget. (Theater owners keep roughly 50% of ticket sales.) The movie could benefit because there hasn’t been an animated offering for families with young kids since September’s “Forgotten Island.” And “Cat in the Hat” won’t have direct competition until Disney’s original “Hexed” launches on Nov. 25.

This is the second adaptation of the Seuss classic following 2003’s live-action comedy, starring Mike Myers as the Cat. That film opened to $38 million, not adjusted for inflation, and ran out of steam with $134 million, a disappointing result given the budget was above $100 million. Bill Hader voices the titular character in the cartooned version, which was directed by Alessandro Carloni and Erica Rivinoja and revolves around the shenanigans that occur after a mischievous cat (wearing a hat) arrives to cheer up two siblings who move to a new town.

“Wild Horse Nine” is catering to older audiences, a demographic that’s been hit or miss in recent years. Searchlight is opting to launch the movie in roughly 1,000 theaters, a larger initial footprint compared to McDonagh’s prior film, 2022’s “The Banshees of Inisherin.” After a start in limited release, “Banshees of Inisherin” became a slow and steady box office winner with $10.5 million domestically and $50 million globally. “Wild Horse Nine,” which similarly hopes to find itself in the Oscar race, follows two CIA officers (Malkovich and Rockwell) who are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island shortly before a Chilean military coup.

This weekend’s other newcomer is the Indian epic “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend,” which is projected to earn $6 million during its first four days in theaters. Those ticket sales are comparable to recent Telugu language fantasy films like “Kalki 2898 AD” ($5.6 million), “Devara Part 1” ($5.6 million) and “Pushpa: The Rule – Part 2” ($5 million) — all of which were released in 2024 and legged out to various degrees. Sony is distributing “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend” in 1,300 theaters, marking the widest North American release for an Indian film.

Grab your high-lumen flashlight and gargantuan gun to explore these vicious vessels

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Abandoned, possessed, or infested spaceships in sci-fi films, books, and video games are usually not a welcoming place to hang your helmet and kick back inside.

Many are distinctly marked as DO NOT APPROACH zones and equipped with clearly articulated warning messages to keep your distance, but that doesn't ever seem to stop scavengers, space pirates, or evil industrial mega corporations from waving off these dangerous signs to board anyway.

Other creaky craft are apt to contain nasty alien hitchhikers or biological hazards not exactly conducive to a pleasant star-trekking voyage. Whether these nefarious neglected craft have just reappeared from the other side of a black hole or have been lying dormant for eons on a hostile planetoid, visitors are usually infrequent.

So ignore those distress beacons at your own peril and step into this alarming armada of 9 nightmarish sci-fi spaceships before orbits decay.

This is not a ranked list, just a collection of our favorites.

It's basically a perfectly good interstellar mining vessel owned by the Concordance Extraction Corporation if you forget about the nasty reanimated corpses found lurking on nearly every deadly deck.

The pesky Necromorphs are a resilient crop of creatures and are extremely inhospitable when it comes to having uninvited guests, yet they don't mind if you're staying for dinner.

This plague of hungry zombified corpses is a real drag, unless you happen to have a flaring plasma cutter in your back pocket and your name is Isaac Clarke.

Things would be much more peaceful aboard the Grendel if a notorious undead slasher named Jason Voorhees wasn't stashed in the cargo bay, but when scientific discovery enters the equation, many questionable choices follow.

The Grendel is a 25th-century medical research vessel on a field trip from hell to an overly polluted Earth, where the frozen Jason is kept at the Crystal Lake Research Facility and shipped back home to Earth 2 for cellular research.

Once thawed, the ship becomes his private killing field with an ample supply of student bodies until the fiery finale when Jason becomes an inhuman meteor in the sky. Next time, take the school bus.

This spooky classic novel written by "2001's" legendary author, Arthur C. Clarke, focuses on a massive alien spaceship entering Earth's atmosphere.

The 31-mile-long cylindrical spaceship does not parallel park easily and is quite spacious inside. In fact, it’s primarily hollow at first and likely offers up a fantastic location for some echoey yodeling. As we later learn, Rama aliens are apparently collecting forms of intelligent life from around the galaxy, employing their ginormous Rama spacecraft.

As an ice ring thaws and forms a vast ocean, astronauts explore the ship’s cavernous confines, only to find automated bio-machines and weird metallic towers, curved alloy cliffs, and fantastic geometric city-like structures. The myriad mysteries that unfold are enough to drive sane humans to absolute madness!

Ignore that glistening brown protomolecular goo, and come on in and sit a spell in the Scopuli, a light Martian freighter used by the Outer Planets Alliance for clandestine missions and ransacked by the evil security firm Protogen in an attempt to hijack its alien cargo.

Hailing from James S.A. Corey's first book in "The Expanse Series", the Scopuli was found moored to an asteroid by James Holden and his Canterbury crew. The amber-brown mess discovered inside the rigged ship is not to be trifled with, let alone inhaled, eaten, or touched.

Come to think of it, it’s probably much wiser to get out while you can and move along!

Anything that looks like an organic hammer-headed horseshoe lying canted in a rocky ravine on a hostile, uncharted planetoid is best to avoid. Especially when its repeating SOS beacon is translated into its true message… a dire warning to keep curious rubberneckers the hell away!

Once its strange, sexually suggestive openings are penetrated by Nostromo crew members, seeing fossilized giants and oceans of squishy egg pods in the cargo hold would make most reasonable people flee in terror.

We're better off leaving this sleeping nightmare in its resting place.

One of the inspirations for Ridley Scott's "Alien", this Golden Age goodie brings us aboard the sleek silver rescue rocketship, Challenge 142, and locks us inside after a bloodthirsty reptilian alien from Mars decides to catch a lift back to Earth with its new astronaut friends in the far-flung future of... 1973!

Mute, clawed monsters with insatiable appetites for human flesh are never good travel companions in the confines of a steel spacecraft. A wiser choice would have been to have stayed on Mars and used the Challenge 142 as a stylized red planet potato farm.

Need a glowing golden suntan? This vessel was launched from Earth to detonate a nuclear payload within the sun's fury to keep its fusion furnace burning and was never heard from again.

A sister rescue vessel, the Icarus 2, was dispatched as a last resort and encountered this long-abandoned ship drifting near the scorching star. Inside the Icarus 1, its over-tanned Captain Pinback has been caught in an addictive ritual of basking in the sun's brilliant embrace and has gone quite insane.

Back out quietly and toss him a nice bottle of aloe vera lotion.

Lawrence Fishburne's Captain Miller thinks this place is a tomb! Well, that's not a very polite way to describe what I think is one of the most ominous spaceships ever seen on screen.

The fact that this foreboding vessel, designed after the cathedral of Notre Dame, has appeared in Neptune's orbit following its disappearance after entering a black hole should be enough to keep the crew of the Lewis and Clark from steering anywhere close. Nothing good can be happening on that doomed craft considering the seven-year absence.

One second after discovering that the craft punctured a route straight to Hades and returned with some extra baggage, I'd be running for the exit hatch! The welcome mat is out, but there's no need to knock on this airlock.

Basically an "Alien" ripoff, this low-budget cult sci-fi flick has its following, but only from those midnight runs to the video store in the '80s to grab the tape with the craziest-looking alien on the cover.

The Shenandoah is a prospecting explorer sent by a ruthless corporation to claim an alien archaeological site on Saturn's moon, Titan. Assorted chaos ensues when a rival West German spaceship is discovered at the dig site, only for our protagonists to find the crew slaughtered.

The carnivorous monster that creeps onto the Shenandoah suffers from little monster syndrome, but its bite is impressive. Best to have never touched the metallic pods in the subterranean cave and just skipped this homicidal mission entirely.

Jeff lives in beautiful Bend, Oregon amid the ponderosa pines, classic muscle cars, a crypt of collector horror comics, and two loyal English Setters.

#711. Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy

A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert after the incident.

A knife-wielding assailant attacked a police guard outside the Israeli Embassy in the Serbian capital, Belgrade, overnight to Wednesday, slightly wounding the officer before being shot dead by him, Serbia's interior minister said.

Interior Minister Ivica Dacic said the attacker, whom he described as a minor, had been monitored by security agencies as a supporter of the terrorist organization "Islamic State" (IS).

Israel's Foreign Ministry later confirmed an "attempted terrorist attack" near its embassy in Belgrade, adding that no personnel were injured and the incident was being investigated.

The attacker was thought to come from the western Serbian town of Sabac and "kept the black flag in support of the 'Islamic State' on his Instagram” account," according to the minister.

Dacic said the assailant shouted "Allahu Akbar," or "God is great" in Arabic, during the attack on the guard. According to Dacic, the guard killed the attacker in self-defense.

He said police were treating the incident as a terrorist attack, with the terrorism threat level raised to its highest, or "red alert."

"This means tighter security checks and an increased police presence at sensitive sites, including infrastructure facilities and places where large crowds gather," he said.

The attack came  just days after key early parliamentary election in Serbia and one day after Israel held its parliamentary vote, with no clear result yet in sight.

In June 2024, an attacker with a crossbow seriously wounded a Serbian police officer guarding the same embassy in Belgrade before being shot and killed by police.

That attacker was identified as a 25-year-old Islamic convert from a village near the capital who had become radicalized.

#709. ‘Dune 3’ Cast Says the Movie Takes ‘Departures’ From the Books, but ‘You’re Crazy If You’re Going to Pick Fault’ With It

The cast of Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune 3” is getting the word out early: There will be major “departures” from Frank Herbert’s literary franchise in the upcoming film, which is set to pull heavily from Herbert’s 1969 sequel novel “Dune Messiah.”

“There’s a lot in this film that is very true to the source material, and there are departures,” Zendaya told The New York Times, with franchise newcomer Robert Pattinson adding: “You got to be kind of crazy if you’re going to be picking fault with this one [over the changes to the books].” Related Stories The Avalanches Create Another Sample-delic Pop Masterpiece With ‘No Bad Memories’: Album Review 'The Mosquito Bowl' Review: Football Heroes Take to the Battlefield in Peter Berg's Emptily Macho WWII Epic

“The script was really cool, but it was quite complicated,” added Pattinson, who makes his “Dune” debut as Scytale. “And watching the film, it’s not about what I thought it was going to be about at all. It reads as much more of a grand political, moral fable, and the movie is so much more emotional. A lot of it is about parenting, and I just thought it was so moving.”

When asked if he was satisfied with Villeneuve’s ending of the film trilogy, franchise star Timothée Chalamet answered: “Absolutely. It didn’t feel like the bar dropped at all, Denis just changed the location of the bar. This movie is its own thing.”

“Dune 3” arrives in theaters at the tail end of a successful year at the box office. It’s opening weekend alongside “Avengers: Doomsday” is widely expected to be the highest-grossing single weekend in box office history. Florence Pugh, who returns in the third movie as Irulan, credits the “Dune” movies with bringing “back moviegoing” following the pandemic and various Hollywood strikes. The first “Dune” movie opened simultaneously in theaters and on HBO Max and grossed $410 million worldwide, no small feat in 2021 when Hollywood was still being disrupted by COVID. The 2024 sequel received an exclusive theatrical release and earned a mighty $714 million.

“What an event the second one was,” Pugh told The Times. “It was just so lovely to be a part of something that we know is our generational kind of ‘Star Wars.'”

Zendaya added, “Any opportunity that we have that we can hopefully contribute to the moviegoing experience and keep that alive, because it’s so much a part of my life, my childhood, so many people’s lives — it’s the reason we do it.”

“Dune 3” opens in theaters Dec. 18 from Warner Bros and Legendary.
